---
### Review: PR #4949 — `ship` skill babysit changes

- [x] Read the diff against `origin/main`
- [x] Read the full `ship` skill for surrounding context
- [x] Check the three claims for internal consistency
- [x] Verify the `gh` commands against the live API
- [x] Post review

All three intents are well-argued and the writing is good — the failure modes named (nit loops stalling the skill, follow-ups proposed after merge) are real, and the anti-patterns table earns its space. The problem is the mechanism in change (1): the poll it replaces `--watch` with **cannot run as written**, and its two stated guards have no data to run on. Change (2)'s cutoff is also counted in a unit that change (1) just redefined.

Findings are inline; summary below.

**Important**

| # | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [L649](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071220117) | `reviewThreads` is **not** a `gh pr view --json` field — verified on the runner, the call exits with `Unknown JSON field`. It was already wrong on `main`, but there it ran once per round behind `--watch`; here it is the loop's only data source. Related: `reviews[]`/`comments[]` carry no commit oid, so the line-650 SHA filter has nothing to read (`gh api …/pulls/{n}/reviews` does return `commit_id`), and the newly-added `headRefOid` is fetched but never used. |
| 2 | [L658](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071221652) | Consumed-by-id inverts against this repo's own bot. `claude-code-review.yml` runs `track_progress: true` — one comment, posted empty at the start and **edited in place** with the finished review (this comment is that comment). So the progress placeholder burns the early break, and the real review, arriving under the same id, is skipped as already-consumed. No `updatedAt` in the payload to key on. |
| 3 | [L684](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071222957) | The cutoff's rationale is "past round 3 each nit costs a full CI cycle", but the early break means a round is no longer a CI cycle. Two quick review comments can reach round 4 after one push, and nits start getting declined early. Count the cutoff on pushes, not iterations. |
| 4 | [L741](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071224145) | 12b's "ship it now → push, let Phase 12's exit conditions re-apply" re-enters a loop that already emitted `babysit_done`, with no statement about the shared round counter, the budget, or whether 12b may run twice. Also lets the disposition question be asked over in-flight checks. |

**Nit** — [L646](https://github.com/skaile-ai/platform/pull/4949#discussion_r4071224985): dropping `skip the watch` makes the empty-`statusCheckRollup` probe the first thing evaluated after a push, which is exactly when a CI-having repo legitimately returns 0; the loop can exit reporting `no-checks` and offer a merge on a suite that never started.

**Things I checked that are fine**

- The closing-keyword rule for follow-up bodies is correct and worth having — GitHub does fire `Closes` from an issue body's cross-reference on merge.
- Skipping the `agent` label on follow-ups is consistent with the rest of the skill (backlog vs. claimed work).
- The missing-label hazard on `gh issue create` is already covered at L316, so the hedged `--label` at L831 is fine as-is.
- No changeset is correct: `.claude/**` is outside the `changeset-check.yml` paths, and `ship` is not in `scripts/embed-builtin-skills.ts`.
- Version bump 1.1.0 → 1.3.0 and the drift note against the `.codex` / ai-assets copies (#4944) — no objection to landing the divergence deliberately.

One unrelated observation, not a PR defect: in this checkout `git status` shows `.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md` as modified at `HEAD`, with the working-tree copy back at `version: 1.1.0`. I reviewed the committed content (`git show HEAD:…`), not the working tree. Runner artifact as far as I can tell, but flagging in case it means something locally.

*Nothing implemented — review only, as requested.*
